# AWE exact construction catalog

This catalog describes exact mathematical constructions for integer matrix products using FP4 products. It contains no performance measurements. Site: https://fp4-is-all-you-need.github.io/AWE/

## Data

- [Version and SHA-256 shard index](index.json)
- [Solution JSON Schema](schema/solution.schema.json)
- [Index JSON Schema](schema/index.schema.json)
- [Compact search metadata](search/index.json)

Use `index.json` as the root of trust: pin its SHA-256 and data_version from an explicitly chosen repository commit. Verify every referenced SHA-256 before parsing. `complete` concerns declared selected input arrays, not completeness of mathematical search or support for every source format.

Within the current input collection, to find a minimum-product construction covering integer widths A and B, read the search index via the hash in index.json. Select groups with width_a >= A and width_b >= B; exclude mixed=true unless mixed storage is intended. Read matching groups with hash verification. Rows are arrays; the search index lists columns. Sort by r and then id. Retrieve an ID awe1_<hash> from solutions/<first two hash characters>.json using its hash in index.json. Counts and minimum product counts apply only to the current input collection, a partial copy of existing results. Missing records do not establish nonexistence, even within a listed width. Do not run new searches to fill gaps.

Widths refer to symmetric ranges [-(2^(M-1)-1), 2^(M-1)-1]. Read domain for exact bounds. `verified.n_pairs` is actual pair enumeration; `n_pairs_proven` is the size of the domain proved by complete encoding plus an exact bilinear identity. Methods distinguish `full_pairs`, `exhaustive_encoding_and_bilinear_identity`, and `coverage_proof_and_bilinear_identity`. The third method requires a machine-checked construction rule and coverage certificate; its checker is not yet implemented and such inputs remain quarantined. An unsupported method never establishes verification. `accumulation.max_k` is a sufficient bound for separately accumulated products with 24-bit integer precision, followed by exact reconstruction.

## Python and figures

Install the local package with `python -m pip install .`. It has no runtime dependency. Use `Catalog(data_directory_or_https_base, version=..., index_sha256=...)`, then `find(a=8,b=8)`, `get(id)`, and `verify(solution)`. A CLI is available as `python -m awe_catalog`.

`awe --data DATA --version VERSION --index-sha256 HASH find --a 8 --b 8 --limit 1`

Use the same prefix followed by `svg ID --output figure.svg`, `tikz ID --output figure.tex`, `matplotlib ID --output figure.py`, or `example ID --a 7 --b -3`. Figure files contain exact cell contributions, plane linear combinations and reconstruction coefficients. The matplotlib source requires matplotlib to render; TikZ source requires a TeX installation with TikZ.

Use `constants ID --output constants.json` to export verified numeric construction data with the version, index hash and immutable ID for an implementing library. This does not configure any GPU kernel.

Two supplied modular sets are now available through the modular reference in index.json; negative results remain pending. Unsupported input formats are excluded; do not interpret them as nonexistent constructions.

## Modular constructions

Follow index.json.modular and then modular/index.json, checking both SHA-256 references, to read modular/catalog.json. The schema is schema/modular.schema.json. Solutions have IDs awem1_<hash>; sets have IDs awems1_<hash>. magnitude_bits M means |A|,|B| <= 2^M-1. This differs from integer widths. Filter magnitude_bits >= requested bits and verification.max_k >= K (parse decimal strings as integers), then rank by products * product_cost + faces * plane_cost, products, ID. Minimum counts apply only to the current input collection.

Each modular solution is checked for a polynomial congruence modulo p, complete per-side residue encoding and all p^2 residue pairs (method full_pairs). Set verification checks pairwise coprimality, P > 2*K*(2^M-1)^2 and separate-product accumulation bounds; reconstruction uses exact integers and centered CRT. These are not integer polynomial equalities or enumeration of all 53-bit integer pairs.

Python: Catalog.find_modular(bits=53,k=16384), get_modular(id), verify_modular_set(id). CLI: find-modular, get-modular, verify-modular-set; per-modulus IDs support verify-modular, example-modular, svg-modular, tikz-modular and matplotlib-modular. Do not send modular records to the integer-only browser import or tier board.

Single modular constructions outside the saved sets: read modular/forms-index.json (schema/modular-forms-index.schema.json), then the chunk files it lists by modulus range, checking each SHA-256; rows follow schema/modular-forms.schema.json with IDs awem2_<hash>. plane_sets names the smallest value set the construction was checked on; value_set_inclusion lists that 2xE2M1 is contained in 8xE2M3 and 16xE3M2, so FP4 constructions also hold arithmetically on FP6. The page toggle keeps the checked value-set collections separate. holes.method=search counts are exact; literal_table counts above 0 are upper bounds. A denominator above 1 is checked only for reconstruction.procedure divide_d1_then_multiply_d2_inverse (sum modulo verified.check_modulus, divide by d1, multiply by d2^-1 modulo m); dividing by the whole denominator is not covered. Constructions the public verifier cannot check are counted in excluded and listed in modular/forms-excluded.json (IDs awem2c_<hash>); their absence from the chunks does not establish nonexistence. prime_powers summarizes the fewest-product rows per prime-power modulus and value set. Recheck with python -m tools.modular_forms check data/modular.

The root input_inventory reference describes input content hashes and duplicate copies, not solutions. Modular intake preserves source selection/table-check labels separately from independent acceptance; search_scopes contains hash-pinned source declarations, not a proof of global exhaustive search. Resolve solution provenance through intake declarations to these scopes.

Verification summaries are available as verification.json (integers) and modular/verification.json (residues and sets). They list checked file hashes, counts, mathematical methods, verification dates and verifier versions. Local ingestion checks produce these records; their consistency alone does not replace mathematical verification. See README for rechecking a checkout without original search inputs.

FP6 saved modulus sets: data/modular/fp6-sets.json (schema data/schema/modular-fp6-sets.schema.json) holds saved CRT sets on the 8xE2M3 value set, for magnitude_bits 53 (20 moduli, 30 products) and 72 (22 moduli, 41 products). Each construction is a schema-2 single-construction record (awem2_ id) with provenance, verified by verify/modular_forms.py on the smallest value set that keeps its holes; 2xE2M1 records hold on 8xE2M3 as integers. The site loads the file with the other modular catalogs, and the modulus-set list labels these sets "FP6 (8×E2M3)". Their K bound is the 24-bit accumulation bound of the constructions, so they are listed when K is at or below it (for example K=4096). Recheck with python -m tools.fp6_sets check.

## Modulo spiral: every integer keeps its position

Open ?section=polar-periodic. Page-wide format: prime_set=fp4|fp6 and periodic_fp6=8xE2M3|16xE3M2. Iterate integer moduli from polar_start (default 2), up to polar_count positions (default 169, including missing entries; default range 2..170), capped at 65536. Missing or filtered constructions keep an unfilled circular mark and no numeric label. Recorded labels remain upright. No text is drawn in the center; the existing detail pane shows the selected modulus.

Parameters: polar_spacing=linear (default)|powers|arc; polar_base=13 integer[2,32]; polar_count=169 integer[1,65535]; polar_start=2 integer[2,65536]; polar_cell_width=24 [8,80] (arc only); polar_spiral_growth=5 [1,12]; polar_inner_radius=36 [24,100]; polar_band_width=0.85 [0.1,1]; polar_taper=0.1 [0,1] (0 means constant thickness); polar_layout=spiral|rings; polar_tier=color|width; polar_color=prime (default)|products|tier; polar_mark=top (default)|thickness|gauge|none; polar_top=10 integer[1,100]; polar_factors=exponent (default)|repeat|none|dots|bands; arc=arith (default)|geom|step; polar_size=products (default)|cost|products_per_bit|constant; polar_composites=all|saving; polar_holes=0 [0,100]; polar_modulus=13 integer[2,65536]; polar_form=<construction id> (empty: the spiral's default construction; an id that is not a candidate of the selected modulus falls back). Invalid values revert to defaults. These controls update the URL. The zoom slider [0.5,64] scales around the diagram center independently of the selected modulus; the existing selected-modulus zoom button remains. Zoom is not persisted in the URL.

Procedural API: integerModuli generates every integer position. ribbonCell computes each sector from turnInterval and angularProfile. Default linear mode assigns B*r integers to turn r; arithmetic or geometric angular widths integrate to exactly 2*pi and join continuously. powers mode retains B^k boundaries; step retains the old uniform widths. The centreline remains r0+b*theta. Band thickness interpolates the endpoint taper values in the same integer coordinate. See docs/URL_CONTROLS.md for the formulas and ranges.

Continuous half-width h(theta)=min(pi*growth*width,0.4*innerRadius)/(1+taper*theta/(2*pi)); polygon vertices offset the centerline normal by h(theta)*widthScale. There is no width step at power boundaries. Area is an approximation from endpoint widths and arc length, not an equal-area guarantee. Arc mode advances one fixed centerline arc length per integer position. Rings remains an optional layout. Counts, hole markings and cost tiers use only the selected catalog records; absent records are not invented.

Compare ?section=polar-periodic&polar_base=10, polar_base=11 and polar_base=13; all use the same smooth taper. Deprecated polar_period,polar_period_bits,polar_end,polar_radius_growth are ignored. See docs/URL_CONTROLS.md.

Molecule-table details: section=composite-table opens the table. molecule_page_size is the page size (default 15, integers 1–100). molecule_modulus selects the composite modulus for an open details panel. The diagram projects the selected minimum-product combined construction onto each coprime prime-power component. It draws a contribution only after checking an invertible denominator, safe plane reductions, and the bilinear coefficient identity modulo that component. Nonunit denominators, unsafe plane reductions and failed coefficient checks are shown as unconfirmed; no shared edges are invented. The independently selected component minima and the projected combined construction can use different encodings. Shared-term counts are not equated with product savings.

## Construction details and legacy links

The former “8×8: holes and plane constraints” section is now part of the construction list (section=modular-forms). data/modular/integer-examples.json preserves all four integer examples, their domain [-128,127], holes, encoding and correction metadata, scoped canonical keys, and legacy aliases. These are not modular constructions and are not counted in the modular catalog. A joint_id URL resolves only through those aliases to forms_id=joint_<id>, selects FP4 and opens the same Expansion. Its existing per-construction display parameters remain valid.

Select a modular construction with forms_id=<published id>. Its row opens Expansion, including holes, plane moduli, available encodings and coefficients. Missing encoding tables remain missing; no new encodings are fabricated.

The FP6 import adds 1,994 verified constructions (1,095 8xE2M3, 899 16xE3M2), after the existing eleven-axis selection. FP4 records are unchanged. The construction list, modulo spiral and composite table switch together. New full cost metadata is unconfirmed; use polar_size=products or products_per_bit for those rows.


Molecule grid: section=composite-table&molecule_modulus=510 selects the combined construction. The default is an A-limb by B-limb grid in stored order. molecule_grid_color=components (default) colours component support and overlap; products uses the same saved-product palette as Expansion. T, plane and limb indices are zero-based saved indices, matching Expansion (T0 is the first saved product). Selecting a cell or T button displays its reconstruction coefficient, A/B plane indices, limb coefficient vectors, used limbs and checked component contributions for the product and each plane. Shared product/plane/limb counts are visible without opening the dependency graph. In products mode the combined grid retains all saved plane supports even when component projections are unconfirmed; per-component grids only show checked contributions. An orange overlapping cell may contain different exclusive products; the dot indicates at least one SAME product contributes to multiple components at that cell. Contributions are checked before cancellation, component by component; unknown projections stay unknown. Per-component grids, existing CompactExpansion and the limb/plane/product dependency graph are in initially closed details. The catalog does not record CRT-2 execution order or intermediate residues, and these are not invented. Candidate section URLs are unchanged; the minimum-products heading now displays both product count N and candidate count M.


Current spiral defaults are based on 169 integer positions, including unrecorded moduli.


FP6 periodic intake: data/visualization/fp6-periodic.json retains every delivered (modulus, value set, family, product count) representative and every source summary. Use prime_set=fp6&periodic_fp6=8xE2M3&section=fp6-families; periodic_fp6=16xE3M2 selects E3M2. The entire page switches format. fp6_family is empty (all) or toom|a0_shared_2prime|general_weight_2prime|p2|p2_holes_paid|p2_karatsuba|p3|polynomial; fp6_m is an exact positive integer modulus or empty; fp6_holes=1 includes holes, 0 requires hole-free; fp6_page is zero-based, 0..10000, 50 rows/page, clamped to the available last page. Family rows display denominator and recon beside hole counts. checked rows link to forms_id; source_only rows are retained in this table but do not enter the verified modulo spiral or component comparisons. General-weight no-hole-free bounds apply only to their recorded search conditions; open cells remain open and bounds do not apply to other families. Source IDs beginning fp6r_ are stable construction-derived public IDs; private execution identifiers are omitted. Both FP4 and FP6 default to powers mode with base 13 and up to 169 cells; arc remains selectable.

Cost-table prototype: section=modulus-cost uses the page-wide prime_set=fp4|fp6 and periodic_fp6=8xE2M3|16xE3M2. cost_sort=cost|products|modulus (default cost); cost_prime=2..65536 prime factor or empty for all; cost_holes=0|1 (default 0); cost_page=0..10000 (default 0), 15 rows/page. Prime-factor colours are stable across formats and filters. Unknown modeled costs stay last as —; these are not measured runtimes or CRT-set rankings. See docs/URL_CONTROLS.md and docs/COLOR_RULES.md.

Modulo spiral update: arc=arith|geom|step (default arith) interpolates angular width and band thickness across each power interval, preserving exact full turns and every integer position. geom uses geometric interpolation; step is the previous per-turn constant angular width for comparison. polar_color=products|tier (default products) sets the in-chart colour legend. products uses ordered product-count bins; tier shares the existing candidate classification. polar_size now defaults to products. See docs/URL_CONTROLS.md and docs/COLOR_RULES.md.

New default turn layout: polar_spacing=linear uses B*r integers in turn r (r starts at 1), with polar_base=B (default 13, range 2..32). Starting modulus is 2, so base 13 starts with 2..14, then 15..40. polar_spacing=powers retains the earlier power boundaries, and arc retains constant arc length. arc=arith remains default width interpolation; geom is optional. Every integer, including an unrecorded modulus, retains its place.

Optional prime-factor count prototypes: polar_factors=none|dots|bands (default exponent, see below). dots draws one small black dot per distinct prime factor; bands uses inner-to-outer radial dividers to partition a cell into that many parts (count-1 internal lines). Counts: 13 and 169 = 1, 143 = 2, 1001 = 3. Existing product/tier colour and geometry stay unchanged, and the same in-chart legend line explains the extra marks. Only recorded coloured cells get the overlay.

Prime-only colouring and products/planes marks: polar_color=prime is the new default. Only prime moduli are filled, each with that prime's colour from the factor badges in the cost and composite tables (primeColors.ts). Prime powers and composites are white with a black edge and their number is plain black (no box); a composite with fewer products than the sum for its coprime prime-power components has one underline per product saved and a thicker cell edge, and is labelled at every zoom (other labels thin out every tickStep positions). polar_mark compares ways to show products and planes without extra colours: top (default) draws a thick box and bold number for the lowest polar_top percent (default 10, rounded up) of cost per bit, cost / log2 m with the cost coefficients; thickness scales band thickness with bits per product, log2 m / products, relative to the best displayed modulus (floor 20%); gauge draws a black bar along each cell's inner edge whose length (share of the cell's arc) is bits per product, and one along the outer edge for bits per plane, log2 m / (planes A + B), both relative to the best displayed modulus (the earlier square value opens gauge); none adds no mark. At zoom 2 or more each cell also shows "products planes A/B". When a modulus has several constructions that no other beats in both products and planes A+B (343: 5 products with 4/4 planes and 6 products with 3/3 planes), the zoomed cell is split radially into one band per such pair, fewest products innermost, with one "products planes A/B" line each under the number. A band shows the spiral's default construction when its pair holds it, otherwise the cheapest undominated construction of the pair (then fewer limbs A+B, then id); clicking a band selects that modulus and construction (polar_modulus, polar_form=<id>). For the selected modulus each line adds how the construction fits the modulus: "w^3,w^4≡0" for weights 1, w, w^2, ... whose powers vanish modulo the modulus, and "plane moduli 7·49" when the source plane_moduli has values below the modulus (folded planes); the candidate list and the detail ("fit to the modulus") say the same. products and tier colouring are unchanged. With polar_color=prime, prime powers and composites also list their prime factors under the number, each in its factor-badge colour: polar_factors=exponent (default) draws one box per prime with the exponent at upper right (72 = 2^3 3^2, 169 = 13^2); repeat draws the prime's box exponent times, wrapping after five (72: 2 2 2 3 3). See docs/URL_CONTROLS.md and docs/COLOR_RULES.md.

Selected composite panel: when polar_modulus (set by clicking a cell) is a composite with fewer products than the sum for its coprime prime-power components, the spiral is followed by the same detail as the composite table (MoleculeDetail: components, the combined construction and its limb-pair grid), headed by a line such as "CRT 9 products -> 7". In the grid, a cell that contributes to several components is hatched in the colours of those components. The comparison is that of the composite table (same value set and hole filter, minimum products, CRT reconstruction cost excluded). Other moduli show no panel.
